text: Independent evidence corroborates the 2021 loss event of 81.3 hectares (2.23% of the asset). The University of Maryland’s Global Forest Change dataset (Hansen GFC) confirmed the loss in 2021, meeting the rule requiring observation in a later year of the series. The European Commission’s JRC Global Forest Cover 2020 dataset validated that 98% of the affected area was forested in 2020, satisfying the 50% agreement threshold. Uruguay’s MGAP National Forest Cartography further specified that the event area was primarily planted forest (68.1 ha) of *Pinus elliottii* and *Pinus taeda*, with no native forest involved. The datasets collectively confirm the event’s location, timing, and nature, while excluding smaller patches (37.3 ha) below the 0.5-ha event threshold.
